map_info.name: Rotation: crossings, arrays and inhabited repetition
map_info.description: One compact hall moves from three full-size centre-pivot crossings to four 2 by 6 rotated cube arrays, then a five-segment hollow tunnel and five smaller carousel profiles. Axis, fixed centre, order, spatial increment and angular speed have distinct encounters.

learning_objectives: Compare Y level crossing with X/Z climbs about fixed centres
Read axis and rotation order in four two-dimensional cube arrays
Distinguish angle distributed through space from angular speed through time
Compare five silhouettes under one angular-speed rule and carry the relation between object size and body into scale

documentation.summary: One compact hall moves from three full-size centre-pivot crossings to four 2 by 6 rotated cube arrays, then a five-segment hollow tunnel and five smaller carousel profiles. Axis, fixed centre, order, spatial increment and angular speed have distinct encounters.
documentation.layout: 39 x 60 source grid. Centre blades at (19,11); arrays at (19,25); central tunnel at (19,42); five 0.4-scale cakes in side niches. Grid banks and return wedges remain physical; side aisles bypass moving geometry.
documentation.objective: Follow one rotation operation from crossing to obstacle to architectural repetition, then distinguish spatial angle from time-driven speed.
documentation.arrival: Standalone: cell (19,2), facing +Z, before the first crossing. Museum uses its own vestibule arrival; grid spawns are stripped.

gallery.removed_duplicate: Second identical cake reference; all five distinct profiles retained.

refresh.preserved: Human-size 8.4m blades, 2.04m array cubes, five carousel profiles, inhabitable full-scale tunnel. Repetition counts shortened; one duplicate cake removed.
